key_insight: Noise-aware scheduling, decoding, and post-selection let a 156-qubit heavy-hex superconducting processor deliver substantially better error-corrected memory and logical operations despite device nonuniformity.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that large monolithic quantum processors can remain useful for fault-tolerant computing even when some qubits or couplers underperform, if control and decoding are adapted to the hardware.
method: Dynamic compass code on a 156-qubit heavy-hex lattice
Exclude worst qubits/couplers and redesign measurement schedules
Use noise-informed decoding plus leakage-aware post-selection
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 35% lower logical memory error and up to 56% better stability-logic performance, with Bell fidelities rising above 77% and above 97% after additional logical gap post-selection.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on filtering and post-selection, so the effective logical throughput and scalability may be reduced by discarded shots and hardware-specific calibration overhead.
paper_title: Error-Corrected Memory and Logic on a Heavy-Hex Superconducting-Qubit Processor
